queue.title: AC13 mandates three denied-winner branches, but the sixth-to-seventh substitution branch is provably unreachable under site-scoped matching
queue.assessedDuring: lens-1.5.0-contract P4 verify finding #10, carried through the P3 fix-cycle
queue.rationale: engine-api.md declares that a denied winner from precedence positions 6-7 substitutes the highest-precedence allowed policy value (byAgent, then byRole, then default). But reaching 6/7 for a dispatch means byAgent and byRole already yielded nothing FOR THAT SITE - which is exactly why resolution fell past them - so under the exact/site-scoped matching AC14 requires, no site-scoped substitute can exist. The unscoped reading would let a dispatch inherit a value the caller wrote for a different agent, contradicting AC14. The fixer resolved this honestly by DECLARING the narrowness rather than deleting the row, because deleting it would regress AC13, which mandates all three branches. Both the fixer and the gatekeeper independently flagged this as a SPEC-level contradiction that BUILD cannot settle: the spec would have to amend AC13 before the row could be removed. Not a fixer failure and not another fix cycle.
queue.suggestedFix: Spec decision: either amend AC13 to two branches and delete the row, or redefine substitution as policy-scoped rather than site-scoped and accept the AC14 tension explicitly.

queue.title: AC6 mandates the abbreviated precedence-chain string that AC12's declare-once rule forbids
queue.rationale: spec.md:105 (AC6) requires lens:capability's supports.resolutionRules to carry model: 'deny->record->byAgent->byRole->default->frontmatter' - six positions, abbreviated. spec.md:121 (AC12) requires the chain to be declared once in engine-api.md as the seven-position form ending in 'harness default', and engine-api.md states in its own words that 'a resolution order stated twice has already begun to fork'. capability/SKILL.md:126 carries the AC6 string, so the two criteria are in direct conflict and the fork has already occurred (position 7 absent, record.model->record, agent frontmatter->frontmatter). This predates every fix cycle and was scored met in verify passes 1 and 2; only pass 3's adversarial probe went deep enough to surface it. BUILD cannot resolve a contradiction between two acceptance criteria.
queue.suggestedFix: Spec decision: either (a) amend AC6 so resolutionRules carries a rule NAME (e.g. 'lens-model-precedence-v1') that points at the canonical declaration rather than restating an order, matching how resolutionRules already names 'huginn-quorum-v1' for verify; or (b) amend AC12 to explicitly exempt the resolutionRules value as an identifier rather than a restatement.

queue.title: Five high-severity P4 findings accepted unresolved at the P4 close-out, pending re-probe against a refreshed plugin cache
queue.rationale: Pass 3 returned 5 high findings: (1) modelPolicy model-id values are type-checked but not value-checked, so {"default":""} clears pre-flight; (2) call-time injectedFinders record validation is scoped to model/effort only, so agent/dimension/readonly/unknown keys escape pre-flight; (3) an unparseable or empty .claude/lens/settings.md has no declared branch; (4) settings.md's outputPath is consumed with no containment check; (5) the live-invocation finding that turned out to be a stale-cache artifact. Findings resting on LIVE SKILL INVOCATION are unreliable for this phase because the installed plugin cache was four hours stale; findings resting on FILE READS are sound. The developer elected at the P4 close-out to stop verifying and let P5 REVIEW weigh these against the diff rather than run a fourth cycle on an unbounded degenerate-input surface.

queue.title: Orchestrator P4 probes that invoke a skill observe the installed plugin cache, not the worktree under test
queue.rationale: VERIFY's premise is that probes exercise the RUNNING system. In this repo the running system for a lens skill is ~/.claude/plugins/cache/apurvbazari-plugins/lens/<version>/, which is a snapshot taken when the marketplace was last updated - not the worktree. During this run the cache froze at 2026-07-31T13:50:51Z while two fix cycles edited the worktree at 15:24Z and 17:23Z, so probes invoking lens:capability received the PRE-fix skill (jq -r '.version', 5232 bytes) while the file on disk carried the post-fix type filter (9309 bytes). Confirmed by the orchestrator invoking the skill and diffing the delivered text against disk. This silently invalidates any live-invocation probe after an in-run edit, and it produced at least one high finding whose stated mechanism (Skill-tool truncation) was wrong.
queue.suggestedFix: Have the VERIFY phase either refresh/point the plugin cache at the worktree before probing, or require probes to state whether their evidence came from a file read or a live invocation so the orchestrator can discount the latter after an in-run edit.

queue.title: The closed error-code registry has no machine enforcement: an invented code validates
queue.rationale: FEN-14. definitions.errorEnvelope types error.code as a bare string, so {'code':'E_MADE_UP'} VALIDATES. The $comment justifies this as declare-once discipline -- but the same release accepted MIRRORING for degradedReasons' 7-code enum and guarded the fork with a parity test in tests/lens/test_engine_api.sh. The two shapes make opposite calls on the same question, and the mirrored one is the one a caller can actually validate against. extra is likewise an untyped object, so the per-code shapes ({missing,have}, {role,agent,resolved,deny}, {input,value,expected}, {path,exit}) are unenforced. Note the registry moved from three codes to four on 2026-08-04 (E_MANIFEST_UNREADABLE, developer-approved), which raises rather than lowers the value of machine enforcement.
queue.suggestedFix: Mirror the code enum into definitions.errorEnvelope and extend test_engine_api.sh's existing degradedReasons parity check to cover it in both directions, exactly as that check already does for the degrade codes.

queue.title: huginn-quorum-v1 diverges from the upstream majority rule the retired paragraph named, and nothing discloses it
queue.rationale: FEN-15. The retired pipeline.md section 5 text named the upstream rule (keep unless refuted > total/2) as the deferred target. The wired rule is STRICTER and disagrees at exactly the tie cases: n=2 refutes=1 and n=4 refutes=2 -- the upstream rule keeps, lens drops. pipeline.md calls out 'ties drop' without saying it is a divergence from the named target, no file under lens/ mentions the upstream rule any more, and the CHANGELOG frames the retirement as 'no behavior change at n=1' -- true, and silent about n>1. lens/CLAUDE.md declares the review-findings contract co-owned with the upstream schema, so a resolution-rule divergence is exactly the class of thing that section exists to coordinate.
queue.suggestedFix: Either disclose the divergence in the CHANGELOG and in pipeline.md section 5 (naming the tie cases where the two rules disagree), or coordinate the rule with the upstream repo the way the dimension enum already is.

queue.title: E_MODEL_POLICY_UNSATISFIABLE's extra cannot express a verifier-floor raise
queue.rationale: FEN-16. One code now covers TWO gates -- modelPolicy.deny and the never-Haiku floor -- but its extra is documented as {role, agent, resolved, deny: []}, described as 'the deny list that rejected that model'. On a floor raise no deny list rejected anything and deny[] may be empty, so the failure is undiagnosable from the envelope -- against section Errors' own promise that nothing has to be recovered by parsing prose. extra.role = 'verifier' is not a discriminator either, because a deny raise on a verifier dispatch carries the same role.
queue.suggestedFix: Add a gate discriminator to extra (e.g. gate: 'deny' | 'floor'), or split the floor raise into its own code. The first is additive and cheaper; both are ask-first against the closed registry.

queue.title: injectedFinders, a 1.3.0 input, is the one pre-existing channel that can now raise -- and the not-raises direction is unpinned
queue.rationale: FEN-17. A call-time injectedFinders record with a malformed model/effort now raises. In 1.4.3 the record shape had no rule for extra keys, so a stray model:123 was ignored. I-2's exemption is qualified to calls carrying no 1.5.0 KEY, and model/effort ON a 1.3.0 record are 1.5.0 keys -- so the channel is technically outside I-2 rather than in violation of it, but a 1.3.0 caller reading 'a 1.4.3-shaped call can never receive an error envelope' will not draw that distinction. tests/lens/test_injected_finders.sh pins the raise; nothing pins the other direction -- that a 1.4.3-shaped record must NOT raise. Every other 1.5.0 input has that guard (verifyVotes' 'Absent never raises', modelPolicy's null/absent exemption).
queue.suggestedFix: Add the missing positive twin: pin that an injectedFinders record carrying neither model nor effort cannot raise, and say so in engine-api.md's injectedFinders row the way the verifyVotes bullets already do.

queue.title: finder-malformed is overloaded across two causes at two stages

Those are different coverage states behind one machine-branchable code, and detail is free-form prose. The CHANGELOG says each code is tied to 'the' governing site that emits it, which reads as one site per code. The 2026-08-04 cycle added a third site (adapter-dispatch.md's normalization backstop), which is the output cause again rather than a new one.
queue.suggestedFix: Either split the record cause into its own code (ask-first against the closed 7-code enum), or state in engine-api.md's degradedReasons row that finder-malformed spans both a rejected output and a dropped record, so a consumer knows the code alone does not tell it which.

queue.title: The layout belt cannot fail on three wire rules it is meant to hold
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: `rules()` in tests/walkthrough/sysmap/check.js (lines 42-66) checks a wire only by testing its straight runs against boxes: it does not ask where the wire ends, does not look at the curved joins between runs, and never reads a label's position. Three mutated copies of the engine pass all 608 states of tests/walkthrough/test_sysmap_engine.sh (re-run on 2026-10-11 against the engine as 1.6.0 ships it). Dropping the run into the target (system-map-engine.js:311) leaves 9,096 of 15,140 wires not ending on their target box. Skipping the slots between ranks (line 303) sends 7,250 curved joins through a box that is not an ancestor. Reserving no room for a label (line 164) puts 778 labels on a box and 5,714 on another label. The shipped engine has none of these faults: the three stronger checks, run over the same fixtures in a scratch harness, count 0 each. So the layout is right today, and a regression in any of the three would pass CI. Four smaller gaps go with this. The crossing count in check.js (lines 30-31) is a copy of the engine's (lines 332-333), so the comparison at line 86 shows only that the two copies agree. No assertion reads a wire's `rev` or checks that unwired boxes are placed in a grid; a mutant of each passes. `node check.js` runs with no time limit, so a hang would block the suite instead of failing it. The belt's greps (test_sysmap_engine.sh:35-37) do not match `#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `outerHTML` or `insertAdjacentHTML`; the engine holds none of them today.
queue.resolution: Before the next change to `layout()`, add three assertions to `rules()`. (1) Each wire's first point lies on the border of one of its two end boxes and its last point on the border of the other; a wire with `rev` true is drawn from its target to its source. (2) For each pair of consecutive runs, the rectangle spanned by the end of the first and the start of the second overlaps no box outside the wire's `path`. (3) Each label's rectangle (the label's text width by 14 px, centred on `lx`, `ly`) overlaps no box outside the wire's `path` and no other label. Then write the crossing count in check.js independently of the engine's code, assert `rev` on a fixture with a cycle and the grid on a fixture with no wires, run the harness under a timeout, and widen the greps.

On 2026-10-11 each of the four fixes the fix wave made to this code was reverted in a scratch copy of the repository and the golden page rebuilt: the one-group-at-a-time measuring in `measure()` (engine line 439), the `warn(e)` call in `off()` (engine line 491), the collapsed-group rules for inferred, changed and peer groups (recipe lines 176-180), and the removal of `outline:none` from `.sys-node:focus-visible` (recipe line 115). `tests/run-all.sh` ended `Ran 81 belt script(s); 0 failed.` each time. The page contract also has three hand-kept copies that no belt compares: the recipe's HTML example, the generator tests/walkthrough/sysmap/build-sample.js (it takes its CSS from the recipe and writes its own HTML), and the selectors `init` reads. With `sys-ghead` renamed in the recipe's HTML example, every belt that reads the recipe still passes; a page written from that example would throw in `measure()` and fall back to the plain view on every map that has a group.
queue.resolution: Any of these, cheapest first. (1) A belt assertion that every class and attribute `init` reads appears in the recipe's HTML block and in the generator's output. (2) A static check on the recipe CSS: `.sys-node:focus-visible` has no `outline:none`, and the `.closed[data-inferred]`, `.closed[data-change=...]` and `.closed.peer` selectors exist. (3) A guard in `measure()` that throws when a closed group's title measures 0 wide, about 50 of the engine's 101 spare bytes; a mis-measure then becomes the plain view with a console line instead of a wrong drawing. (4) A headless-browser job in CI that opens tests/walkthrough/fixtures/sysmap-sample.html and, for each map and each one-click state, checks that every visible group's title strip lies inside its box and that the page logs no error.

queue.title: The engine-insert command mishandles a backslash in the engine path and a few unusual page paths
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: All of this is the one-line command at walkthrough/skills/render/references/render-contract.md:65, re-run on 2026-10-11 with macOS awk (version 20200816). (a) It hands awk the engine path with `-v f=`, and awk processes backslash escapes in such a value. With the engine in a directory named `a\tb`, `C:\Users\name` or `plain\qdir`, the shell's `[ -r ]` test passes and the command then exits 1 with nothing on stderr; the page is untouched and no temp file is left. The model is left to type the 28 KB engine. This is rare on macOS and Linux and would be every run with a native Windows path; walkthrough/README.md lists it under Limitations. (b) It writes through the fixed name `<PAGE>.tmp`. A file already at that name is overwritten and consumed on success and deleted on failure. A page that is a symbolic link is replaced by a regular file, and the link's old target keeps its marker line. A page with mode 600 comes out 644 under umask 022. A relative page path shaped like an awk assignment (`x=1.html`) is read by awk as one, so the command exits 1; `./x=1.html` works. (c) tests/walkthrough/test_sysmap_insert.sh has only run on macOS awk. Its first run on a Linux awk is the first CI run of the 1.6.0 pull request, on `ubuntu-latest`.
queue.resolution: Pass the engine path through the environment instead of `-v` (`E="$ENGINE" awk 'BEGIN{f=ENVIRON["E"]} ...'`), and add a directory with a backslash to `HOSTILE` at test_sysmap_insert.sh:59 so the belt holds it. For (b), either state the four cases in the contract as limits, or make the temp file with `mktemp` beside the page and keep the page's mode; the command has to stay one line, because the belt takes it out of the doc and runs it. For (c), read the insert belt's result in the first CI run before relying on the command on Linux.

queue.title: Design and policy questions the 1.6.0 review left to the owner
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11

That works, and it needs python or node and a writable `/tmp`. (2) Headless runs and the default folder. In the tenth run the model called the Write tool on the default path, was refused, and ended with no page. That limit has its own entry: SYSMAP-headless-default-path-writes-no-page. (3) Automatic routing. `/walkthrough:document <repository root>` on a repository with a build or deploy manifest that is neither a plugin nor the marketplace dispatches two opus agents and draws a system map without being asked for one. The README and the changelog now say so. (4) Cost. The six live code-reading runs cost $1.19 to $2.00 each and took 202 to 348 seconds (a sonnet main loop and the two opus agents). (5) Every page with a system map carries about 1.1 KB of CSS for the two retired diagrams (components/system-map.md:207-216), though `update` turns old markup into a system map and no producer writes it any more. (6) No screen-reader pass has been made on a system map: boxes are absolutely positioned, so reading order is the HTML order, and groups carry no role. (7) Layout on very large graphs is untested: the largest fixture has 35 boxes in 8 groups with 46 connections, and the engine skips its second ordering pass from 200 wires up. (8) Two links in opposite directions between the same two closed groups stay two wires, because the engine merges per ordered pair (system-map-engine.js:92; tests/walkthrough/sysmap/check.js:128 pins it), while the README says several connections between two closed boundaries merge into one. (9) A caller outside this repository that passes `walkthrough:document` a second argument not ending in `.html` now gets the page at the default path and a sentence saying why; no such caller could be checked from here. (10) How the routing and the labels look, beyond what the checks measure (boxes that overlap or leave their group, wires that pass through a box), was not judged. (11) `update` reads the whole page back to rebuild its model, and a page with a system map is about 28 KB larger; what that adds to the cost and time of an update was not measured.
queue.resolution: The owner decides each; none blocks 1.6.0. For (1) the choice is a sentence in render-contract.md's write stage: use the Write tool, or a script is acceptable. (2) is decided in its own entry. For (5), the block can go once no supported page predates 1.6.0. For (8), either word the README by direction or merge both directions and draw two arrowheads. For (9), check the owner's other repositories that call the skill.

queue.title: Whether a model follows the code-reading rules is checked only by hand, in live runs
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: The rules that keep a secret or an unverified claim off a code-read map are instructions to a model (walkthrough/references/system-reading.md, the two agents, adapters/system.md). The belts pin their wording; only a live run shows whether a model follows them. Four headless runs of `/walkthrough:document . architecture` were made on 2026-10-11, for $5.66 in all. Three came before the last change to three of the prompt files they exercise (walkthrough/skills/document/SKILL.md and, under its references/, adapters/system.md and gather-subject.md): two on a small fixture repository and one on this repository. The fourth came after that change, on the fixture. One sentence was added to rule 6 after all four (see the end of this note), so no run has been made at exactly the text 1.6.0 ships. Each transcript was checked for seven things. (1) Both agents dispatched by name. (2) No read of a real `.env`; on the fixture, a canary value planted in its gitignored `.env` found nowhere in any tool call, tool result, model text or page. (3) Every content search given a scope that leaves the never-opened paths out: one file, or one folder with a glob that names files or file types. (4) After the agents returned, no read or search of the subject by the main loop, apart from the manifest that Step D of the adapter has it read for the tagline and the links. (5) Directories left unopened because of the depth reported as `out-of-depth`, not `over-budget`. (6) The request word read as a request, not as an output path. (7) The reading line and a Gaps section on the page, the engine inserted, the per-map checks of tests/walkthrough/sysmap-smoke.sh passing on the written page, and no page error in Chrome. In the three earlier runs all seven held, with two limits: one fixture run wrote no page (SYSMAP-headless-default-path-writes-no-page), so (7) was seen in two; and (3) and (5) were only exercised at scale by the run on this repository, where the agents made six searches, each scoped to one file or to one folder with a glob, and all eleven gaps were `out-of-depth`. In none of the three did the main loop go back into the subject after the agents returned (on this repository it read only the skill's own reference files). In the fourth run (1), (2), (6) and (7) held. Its agents made no search (one listing, 16 reads) and its two gaps were the denied `.env` and a README conflict, so it says nothing about (3) or (5). On (4), after the verdicts the skill read one file of the subject, `web/package.json`, which is that manifest read. It read nothing else of the subject and confirmed no anchor. So the two checks that need a large tree, scoped searches and `out-of-depth`, have not been run since that change. The change made after the earlier runs also reworded the clause (4) rests on, and (4) has been seen to hold at the new wording once, on the fixture. On 2026-10-10, before the fix wave, runs on the same two subjects had failed (3), (4) and (5): a search from the root with the glob `{onboard,notify,handoff,walkthrough,lens}/**`, which kept to the five plugin folders but named no file type and excluded nothing inside them, and another of a bare folder; the main loop reading subject files after the verdicts; and twelve directories labelled `over-budget` when 13 of the 60 files the budget allows had been read. Two more things the runs showed that no check looks for. In two of the four runs the model looked for example page markup in the repository the plugin was loaded from. In one, a shell search for a class name went through every `*.html` file under that repository's root. The first five names it returned included two gitignored rendered pages under `.claude/walkthrough/` folders, which .gitignore marks as possibly holding session content; the model then opened only the golden test page (tests/walkthrough/fixtures/sysmap-sample.html). In the other, the same search made with the search tool returned tracked pages only, and the model opened a published page under site/ and the golden test page. An installed plugin has none of these beside it; it suggests the recipe's own example was not enough for the model to build from. And rule 6's check before a search rests on a listing of file names, which can be cut short. In the three fixture runs the agent's listing did show the gitignored `.env`. In the run on this repository the root listing stopped at 100 of 1,076 names and did not show two gitignored `.env` files then in the tree. Both were copies of the fixture's `.env` and held its canary value. The six searches did not reach them: each was scoped to one file or to one folder with a glob, none over a folder that held either file, and the canary is nowhere in that transcript, so neither file was read or matched. One sentence was added to rule 6 for this after the last run, and it has not been run live. What it leaves open, and what the runs show about the search tool and gitignored files, is in SYSMAP-search-rule-limits. Nothing repeats these runs, so a later edit to a prompt can undo a rule with every belt green.
queue.resolution: Owner's call whether to keep a script for this in the repository and run it before a release that touches the reading rules (about $1.20 to $2 a run), and whether to run it once on a large repository at the shipped text before 1.6.0 is released. To rebuild it: a fixture repository with a compose file naming three services, a database, a cache and a queue; two entry points that open them; a `.env.example`; a gitignored `.env` holding a canary value; and a README that contradicts the compose file. Run `claude -p "/walkthrough:document . architecture out/map.html" --plugin-dir <walkthrough> --setting-sources project --max-turns 80 --model sonnet --output-format stream-json --verbose --no-session-persistence`, with Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, Bash, Agent, Task and Skill allowed. These are the flags every run used; `--setting-sources project` decides which settings and hooks load. Load the plugin from a copy that has no `tests/` or `site/` beside it, so the model has only what an installed plugin ships. Then read the transcript: list every Grep with its path and glob, list every main-loop Read, Grep, Glob and Bash call after the last agent result, and search every tool call, tool result and text for the canary. For (3), (5) and the sentence added to rule 6 the subject has to be large enough that the agents search it, leave directories unopened and get a listing that is cut short, with a `.env` holding a canary in a folder they are likely to search. That run shows whether an agent given the new sentence still searches a folder its listing does not cover. It does not show what the search tool does with a file in its scope unless an agent breaks the rule; a direct search settles that (SYSMAP-search-rule-limits).

queue.rationale: walkthrough/skills/document/SKILL.md, Step 1: the output path is the last argument, and only when it ends in `.html`; everything else after the subject is the request. Step 10 adds a closing note when the arguments read as the request drew nothing. What is left: (a) the note is keyed on those arguments as a group (lines 129-131), so `/walkthrough:document . architecture out` routes on `architecture`, drops `out` and says nothing; (b) the note says an output path must end in `.html`, not that it must also be last; (c) a request whose last word ends in `.html` (`... explain index.html`) is taken as the output path, and the page is written to that file; (d) the note also fires for a genuine request on the plugin, marketplace and generic routes, because only the system adapter reads a request at all, and nothing says what a request does on the other routes; (e) the note is in neither walkthrough/README.md nor the changelog; (f) the belt's pin on the rule (tests/walkthrough/test_doc_contracts.sh:247) stops before the sentence's full stop, so a widening added after `.html` stays green; (g) callers outside this repository were not checked. queue.title: The render-check belt is flaky, and one copy of it can kill the Chrome renders of another
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: tests/release-docs/test_render_check.sh drives headless Chrome through .claude/skills/release-docs/scripts/render-check.sh and runs in CI with every other belt (tests/run-all.sh). It is not a walkthrough belt. During the 1.6.0 work it failed three times, each time inside a full-suite run and in a different case each time: exit 143 in the `T5-FONTS-REAL` cases; `T5-POST-BASELINE unchanged overflow passes post-checks`, which expected 0 and got 1; and exit 143 in `T5-BASELINE`. The second failed once more when the belt was rerun by itself straight afterwards, while another Chrome with automation flags had been running on the machine for 41 minutes. Nothing was recorded about what else was running during the first and the third. Every other run passed, by itself and inside the suite. Exit 143 is a kill by SIGTERM, and the belt has a line that sends one to processes it did not start: line 140 runs `pkill -f "render-check\."`, a pattern that matches every `render-check.sh` process and every Chrome whose profile lies under a `render-check.XXXXXX` temp folder, whichever run started it. render-check.sh itself kills only the Chrome it started: by pid (line 102) and by a pattern on its own temp folder (lines 75 and 103). The suite runs its belts one at a time, so this needs two runs on one machine. On 2026-10-11 two copies of the belt were started 60 seconds apart and both failed with `got [143]`, one in a `T5-FONTS` case and one in `T5-GOOD`; started 110 seconds apart, both passed. Which case fails depends on where the other copy is when line 140 runs, which fits a different case each time. It is not shown to be what caused the three failures. render-check.sh also gives each Chrome run `RENDER_TIMEOUT` seconds (30 by default) and retries once, so a loaded machine can run a render out of time as well.
queue.resolution: Scope the kill at line 140 to what that case started: run that one invocation with `TMPDIR="$SCRATCH"`, so that its temp folder lies under the belt's own scratch directory, and `pkill -f` on that path. Then start two copies of the belt 60 seconds apart and see both pass. If it still fails on a busy machine, look at `RENDER_TIMEOUT` in the cases that use real Chrome.

queue.title: A headless run with no output path can end with no page
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: The default output folder is `.claude/walkthrough/` (walkthrough/skills/document/SKILL.md, Step 7; walkthrough/README.md, "Where files go"). In a headless run (`claude -p`, with the Write tool allowed) Claude Code would not let the Write tool write a page there: it asked for permission to edit what it called a sensitive file, and in a headless run nobody is there to give it. That protection of `.claude/` is Claude Code's own and is older than 1.6.0. So a headless `/walkthrough:document` with no output path can do all of its reading and then write nothing. One of the four runs on 2026-10-11 did: both agents ran, the page was assembled, the write was refused, and the run ended by asking where to put the file. The same command with an output path outside `.claude/` wrote its page. The other nine of the ten live runs (2026-10-10 and 11) did not use the Write tool for the page. In each the model wrote a Python or node script under `/tmp`, built the page with it and wrote or copied the page into place with the shell. Five of the nine put their page under `.claude/walkthrough/` that way and were not refused. So whether a headless run on the default path ends with a page depends on which tool the model picks.
queue.resolution: Owner's call. The choices: a README sentence saying that a headless run needs an output path outside `.claude/`; a default outside `.claude/` when nobody is there to approve a write (the plugin already offers a visible `walkthroughs/` folder in a directory that is not a git repository); or a rule that a refused write falls back to that folder and says so. Which tool writes the page is item 1 of SYSMAP-owner-calls-from-the-review.

queue.title: Departures of 1.6.0 from the approved design that are recorded only in this entry
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: None of these is a fault. Each is a departure from the approved design that the owner has not been asked about, and this entry is the only place that records it as one. The reviews found the first four. (1) The "How this was read" grid on a code-read page has no item for how the engine was put into the page; the approved design listed one. The route is only known after the page is written, and the closing message carries it (walkthrough/skills/document/references/adapters/system.md, Step D; walkthrough/skills/document/SKILL.md, Step 10). (2) The two agents are dispatched with `root`, `depth`, `containers`, `rules` and with `root`, `claims`, `rules` (adapters/system.md, Step B). The design had `{root, depth, budget}` and `{root, claims}`; the budget now lives in rule 3 of walkthrough/references/system-reading.md. (3) The reading rules hold more than the design's nine: a tenth rule for ids and labels, an opening paragraph that says what is read is data and not instructions, the gap reason `out-of-depth`, and, under "never opened", searching and citing as well as reading. The adapter also has a row for a claim with no verdict, and takes "containers", "components" and "how it fits together" as requests for a map (walkthrough/skills/document/references/gather-subject.md routes on all three), where the design named only the architecture and the system map. (4) The changelog's "Removed" line names the two retired diagrams in words and carries no backticked class name, where the design said to name them by class name. That was deliberate: the release-docs detector reads a backticked name in a retiring changelog sentence as a retired name (.claude/skills/release-docs/scripts/docs-lib/stale.py), and with none there it reports no candidate for the 1.6.0 range. Two more differences from the design have entries of their own: the reference table has no evidence column (SYSMAP-box-evidence-not-in-plain-view), and wires merge per direction (SYSMAP-owner-calls-from-the-review, item 8). The golden test page was built with four maps where the design planned two, and the fix wave added a fifth. The fix wave made further departures of its own. Each is in the shipped files as behaviour, and some are in the changelog or the README; none is recorded as a departure anywhere else. A map that falls back to the plain view says why in the browser console. An inferred group carries the word "inferred" in its title strip. The reading rules bind the skill as well as the agents, and a skill that cannot read them stops and builds no page. For a code-read map the coverage critic checks the model against the surviving claims and the gaps, never the code. When a group is dropped its children move up, and nothing is dropped by cascade. A detail's `related[]` leaves out a link that closes a loop. After the subject, the output path is the last argument, and only when it ends in `.html`. Self-check rows 1, 6, 24 and 25 were reworded for pages with a map. Three parts of item 3 came from the fix wave as well: the paragraph on data and instructions, the reason `out-of-depth`, and searching and citing under "never opened".
queue.resolution: The owner reads the list and strikes any difference they do not want. One that stays needs nothing more.

queue.title: Rule 6's remedy for an incomplete listing does not keep every never-opened file out of a search
queue.source: walkthrough system map (1.6.0), whole-branch review and fix wave, 2026-10-10 and 11
queue.rationale: Reading rule 6 (walkthrough/references/system-reading.md) says every content search leaves the never-opened paths out: choose a scope, check it against a listing of file names, and never search the whole root unfiltered. A sentence added late in the 1.6.0 work says what to do when the listing is not complete for the place to be searched, as when a listing of a large tree is cut short: search one file, or use a glob for the file types you mean, and never a bare folder. It was added because in a live run on this repository (2026-10-11) the agent's root listing stopped at 100 of 1,076 names and did not show two gitignored `.env` files that were in the tree. That run's six searches were each of one file or of one folder with a glob, and none reached either file. The remedy has two limits. (1) A glob for a file type does not keep every never-opened file out. It keeps out `.env` itself and the key files the rule names by extension. It does not keep out `.env.<anything>`, `id_rsa*`, `secrets.*` or `credentials*`, which take any extension (`secrets.yml` fits `*.yml`), and it does not keep out a dependency or build folder below the folder searched: in that run a `*.md` glob over one folder returned files two folders down. With an incomplete listing the rule's own check, that the scope matches none of these paths, cannot be made for the glob either, so in those cases only the rule's last line is left: discard such a result unread. (2) The sentence names a listing that was cut short. A listing made with a pattern shows only some names by design and is just as unable to show that a folder is clean, and the reader has to infer that it counts as incomplete. Two of the three listings in that run were of that kind. What the runs show about the search tool: once, in the last run of 2026-10-11, the skill searched the repository the plugin was loaded from with the tool, from the root, for `*.html` files holding a class name. The result counted ten files and named five, all tracked, and ten tracked pages hold that string. 55 gitignored pages holding it were under the same root, one of them with no hidden folder in its path and one under an `out/` folder, which rule 6 lists; the count leaves no room for any of them. So the tool left gitignored files out, in one search. Not shown: what the tool does with a hidden file that is not gitignored, and any search with a `.env` itself in scope. A shell search is another matter. The one that ran, a `grep -r` for `*.html` from the same root in an earlier run that day, did return gitignored pages. That is true of that run only: in a later session the same command returned just the ten tracked pages, because that session's `grep` applied ignore files. The two agents have no shell; the skill does. On what was seen, then, a gitignored `.env`, the usual case, is kept out by the tool as well as by the rule, while a `.env` that is committed, and any search made through the shell, has only the rule. No belt pins the new sentence (SYSMAP-belt-pins-could-be-wider), and no live run has been made with it (SYSMAP-live-check-is-by-hand).
queue.resolution: Close the limit in the rule, then pin the sentence and run it. Three ways to close limit 1: have the place to be searched listed in full first, so that the rule's own check can be made; use an exclusion that the search tool applies, if it has one; or search named files only. The first two cover both halves, the names and the folders. Naming files covers the names only: a named file such as `package.json` still matches inside a dependency folder. For limit 2, say in the rule that a listing made with a pattern is not complete either. What is not shown needs no model run: one search with the tool, for a string in the file, over a folder that holds a `.env` that is not gitignored. Whether an agent follows the new sentence needs a live run on a large repository (SYSMAP-live-check-is-by-hand).

queue.title: The engine insert writes to a temp file with a predictable name
queue.source: walkthrough 1.6.0, PR #142 automated reviews (2026-10-14)
queue.rationale: Security review L1. The insert command in walkthrough/skills/render/references/render-contract.md writes awk's output to "$PAGE.tmp" with a plain > redirect, which follows a symbolic link. Someone who can write to the output folder could plant page.html.tmp as a link and have the redirect overwrite its target. That needs write access to the user's own output folder, so the risk is low. mktemp in the same folder would close it, at the cost of a longer command that is pinned by test_sysmap_insert.sh and test_doc_contracts.sh and was run live.
queue.resolution: Switch the temp file to mktemp "$PAGE.XXXXXX" in the same folder, keep the no-temp-file-left check, update the pins, and run the insert belt on macOS and Linux.

queue.title: A relative page path containing = or starting with - makes the engine insert fail
queue.source: walkthrough 1.6.0, PR #142 automated reviews (2026-10-14)
queue.rationale: Security review L2, both cases reproduced on macOS. With PAGE='a=b.html' awk takes the operand as a variable assignment and reads stdin, so the command exits 1, removes the temp file and leaves the page untouched, and the engine is then typed. With PAGE='-x.html' awk reads the file, but mv and then rm take the path as an option and fail, so the command exits 1, the page is untouched, and -x.html.tmp is left behind. In the live runs the skills passed a full path, which starts with /, and the relative defaults they build start with a folder name, so neither case is expected in practice. The PR's Limits name only the backslash case.
queue.resolution: Pass "./$PAGE" when the path is relative, which covers both cases, or name = and a leading - beside the backslash in the contract's limits; pin whichever is chosen in test_sysmap_insert.sh.

queue.title: The docs bot's own post-checks fail the system-map belts on a package.json only its job has
queue.source: release docs run 38523951680 for the walkthrough 1.6.0 release (PR #143, docs PR #144), 2026-10-14
queue.rationale: In the sync job, post-checks from the sealed copy reported 'tests/run-all.sh (Ran 82 belt script(s); 2 failed.)': test_sysmap_engine.sh ('the engine does not parse') and test_sysmap_insert.sh. The model's own node --check of the engine failed with 'Error: Invalid package config /home/runner/work/claude-plugins/claude-plugins/package.json'. The repository tracks no package.json, and the publish job's authoritative post-checks, on a fresh checkout with the same patch, passed run-all. So the sync job's tree held an untracked package.json that node could not parse, and node reads the nearest package.json before it runs any .js under the repository. Most likely it is an empty mount point left by the Bash sandbox, as it leaves for the protected dotfiles; that is not confirmed. The two belts are the first in the suite to run node on a file inside the repository, so from 1.6.0 on every docs PR opens as a draft labelled needs-owner even when the authoritative checks pass.
queue.resolution: Confirm what the file is in a dry run (list it in the trail step). Then either have the sync job's post-checks skip or neutralise sandbox mount points before run-all, or have the two belts run node on a copy outside the repository (or with an explicit --input-type) so a stray package.json cannot reach them.

queue.title: CLOSED: the system-map belts set their own module scope, so an empty package.json in the docs bot's checkout no longer fails them; supersedes PR144-1
queue.source: PR144-1 fix: probe dry run 38556440208 of release-docs.yml from a throwaway branch (2026-10-14)
queue.rationale: PR144-1 guessed where the stray package.json came from. A probe step, run once just before the sealed post-checks in a dry run from a throwaway branch, showed it: /home/runner/work/claude-plugins/claude-plugins/package.json, an empty regular file owned by runner and written during the model's run. Beside it were empty files for .env and its variants, .npmrc, .yarnrc, .yarnrc.yml, bunfig.toml, .gitmodules, package.json, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, node_modules/ and .claude/commands/, all of which git reported as ignored (this repository's .gitignore lists only node_modules/ of them, so the rule came from elsewhere; its source was not printed). The probe run had no docs work to do (0 open obligations) and still failed the same two belts, so any run of the model leaves these files. They look like the Bash sandbox's placeholders for the names it write-protects, but the sandbox lists in the Claude Code 2.1.299 binary checked here do not name package.json, so their exact source is not confirmed. Node read the empty package.json on its way up from the engine and stopped with 'Invalid package config'. The fix: tests/walkthrough/sysmap/package.json pins the module scope of the harness scripts, and test_sysmap_engine.sh checks the engine as a copy beside a package.json of its own and fails if the tracked one is missing. On a copy of the repository under a parent folder holding an empty package.json, and again with one at the repository root, develop's two belts failed with node's error and the fixed ones passed.
queue.resolution: Fixed in the walkthrough belts by the PR that adds tests/walkthrough/sysmap/package.json. The placeholder files themselves are PR144-2.

queue.title: The docs bot's trusted post-checks runs beside empty, git-ignored files the write fence cannot see
queue.source: PR144-1 fix: probe dry run 38556440208 of release-docs.yml from a throwaway branch (2026-10-14)
queue.rationale: After the model's run, the sync job's checkout holds empty files for .env and its variants, .npmrc, .yarnrc, .yarnrc.yml, bunfig.toml, .gitmodules, package.json, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, yarn.lock, node_modules/ and .claude/commands/. Git reports them as ignored, and the write fence lists only changed and untracked paths (git status --untracked-files=all), so it does not see them, and the sealed post-checks runs every belt with them in place. The empty package.json already failed two belts (PR144-1). Others could change what a tool does, such as an empty .npmrc, bunfig.toml or .gitmodules, and a file the model writes under any ignored path is just as invisible to the fence. The publish job re-runs every check on a fresh checkout and publishes only the fenced patch, so nothing reaches a docs PR this way; the sync job's verdict only decides whether the docs PR opens as a draft. Not checked: whether the snapshot taken before the run records ignored files.
queue.resolution: Have the sealed post-checks, or the fence, list the ignored files the run created (git status --ignored against a listing taken before the model runs) and remove or report them before any belt runs; find where the ignore rule for the placeholders comes from.
